# UAT 02-01 runbook: the package review on two machines

Every command below is for you to run. `pc1` is the source, `pc2` the target; every title, answer and message prints those two hostnames, and "source" or "target" naming a machine anywhere you read is a finding.

## 1. Machines

Acquire the Hetzner label lock yourself and release it yourself; never run `lock.sh clear`.

```bash
cd /home/janfr/dev/pc-switcher
export HCLOUD_TOKEN="$(pass show dev/pc-switcher/testing/hcloud_token_rw)"
tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh status
tests/integration/scripts/internal/lock.sh acquire "janfr-uat-02-01"
export PC1="$(hcloud server ip pc1)"
export PC2="$(hcloud server ip pc2)"
for h in "$PC1" "$PC2"; do
  ssh testuser@"$h" 'curl -sSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/flaksit/pc-switcher/refs/heads/main/install.sh | bash -s -- --ref gsd/phase-02-package-management-sync'
done
ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'bash -s -- --with-app' < tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh
ssh testuser@"$PC2" 'bash -s' < tests/integration/scripts/internal/vm-test-fixtures.sh
ssh testuser@"$PC1" '~/.local/bin/pc-switcher init --force'
ssh testuser@"$PC1" 'printf "logging:\n  file: DEBUG\nsync_jobs:\n  apt_sync: true\n  snap_sync: true\n  flatpak_sync: true\n  manual_installs_sync: true\n  folder_sync: true\nfolder_sync:\n  folders:\n    - path: /home\n      enabled: true\n      filter_file: ~/.config/pc-switcher/home.filter\n" > ~/.config/pc-switcher/config.yaml'
```

`init` is run for the two starter filter files it ships, and the config it writes is replaced on the next line. `/home` is the mirrored folder because both files this runbook watches the boundary at live under it — `~/.config/pc-switcher` and `~/snap` — and `home.filter` is what keeps each machine's own `authorized_keys`: a mirror of pc1's would lock the sync out of pc2.

## 2. Diverge the two machines

On pc1, the hold on `sl` is a hold on a package pc1 has, so it travels with the install and is never a question. The four filesystem fixtures are one scan case each: `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` holds a file, so it is the finding; `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` holds two directories and no file, so only you can say what it is; `/opt/pcsw-uat-empty` holds nothing anywhere beneath it; `/usr/local/share` is not scanned at all. The symlink in `/usr/local/bin` is put on both machines, so pc2 already holds it and it is never presented. The two `~/snap/hello` revision directories are the mirror's snap boundary: the run moves pc2 off the second revision and onto pc1's, so by the time the mirror asks pc2 which revisions it holds, pc1's is the only `hello` revision it can name.

```bash
ssh -t testuser@"$PC1"
sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y sl cmatrix tree
sudo apt-mark hold sl
apt-cache policy sl | head -2                    # note pc1's installed version of sl
snap list hello                                  # note pc1's revision of hello
snap info hello | sed -n '/^channels:/,$p'       # pick a second revision, in parentheses, other than pc1's; pc2 is put on it below
mkdir -p ~/snap/hello/<pc1's revision> ~/snap/hello/<that second revision>
touch ~/snap/hello/<pc1's revision>/uat-converged ~/snap/hello/<that second revision>/uat-stray
ln -sfn <pc1's revision> ~/snap/hello/current
sudo mkdir -p /opt/pcsw-uat-app /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/alpha /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/beta /opt/pcsw-uat-empty
echo hi | sudo tee /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/alpha/run /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor/beta/run >/dev/null
sudo touch /usr/local/share/pcsw-uat-note
sudo ln -s /opt/pcsw-uat-app/README /usr/local/bin/pcsw-uat
printf 'allow *\n' > /home/testuser/uat.filter && flatpak remote-modify --user --filter=/home/testuser/uat.filter flathub
exit
```

On pc2: recording `fortunes` as pc2's own makes it invisible to the review and protected as collateral; the filter on `flathub` is pc2's own and excludes the application pc1 has; of the two repository files pc1 does not have, one is used by nothing and one feeds everything pc2 has; and `hello` is moved off pc1's revision so the run has a revision to converge.

```bash
ssh -t testuser@"$PC2"
sudo DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive apt-get install -y fortunes cowsay tree
sudo apt-mark manual fortunes-min
apt-get -s remove -y fortunes-min | grep '^Remv'    # must list fortunes-min AND fortunes
mkdir -p ~/.config/pc-switcher
printf 'machine_specific:\n  "apt:package:fortunes":\n    item_class: apt_package\n    label: fortunes\n    reason: null\n    recorded_at: "2026-07-30T00:00:00+00:00"\n' > ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml
sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/99-pcsw-uat.sources >/dev/null <<'EOF'
Enabled: no
Types: deb
---

149:- The collateral question is titled `Removing fortunes-min on pc2 would remove fortunes`, and the line under that title — above the keys, not under the row — says it is protected on both grounds, naming `pc2` as the machine the mark is on. It names `fortunes` and offers three answers on one row: the act `<y>`, hinted `remove fortunes-min from pc2, so fortunes is removed as well`; `skip now` `<s>`; and `stop the sync` `<q>`, hinted `nothing more is changed on pc2; what earlier jobs already did stays done`. There is no `<x>`.
168:grep -E 'reviewed cowsay|reviewed fortunes \(report_only\)' "$LOG"   # "marked as this machine's own", then "applied"
185:dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${Version} ${Status}\n' sl cmatrix fortunes fortunes-min
194:`sl` is installed at pc1's version and `cmatrix` is absent; `fortunes` and `fortunes-min` are both gone, the collateral answer having taken them; both `.sources` files are still there; `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` exists with its `README`, the snippet having replayed in the run that authored it, and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` does not — it is pc1's own.

2	and never synced (D-08, D-08a, D-09).

4	An entry recorded here means "inert on THIS machine in both roles": not pushed when
5	this machine is the source, not installed or removed when this machine is the target.
6	D-19's whole argument for scanning aggressively — a finding produces noise exactly
7	once, then never again — only holds if this durability is real.
8	
9	Which machine's file gets an entry follows which machine HOLDS the item (D-08a): an
10	install declined for good is recorded on the source, the only machine that has it; a
11	removal and an overwrite are both recorded on the target, which is the machine whose
12	copy the answer keeps. An overwrite is therefore the one direction whose mark can be
13	sitting on either machine when a later run reads it, since the run that recorded it may
14	have been launched the other way round — `PackageSyncJob._mark_holders` is where that
15	asymmetry is stated once, for the write and the read together. Because the file is
16	machine-local, the write must land on the correct END of the connection — on the
17	target this means going through the remote executor, never a local `pathlib` write
18	(ADR-002: the target has no direct filesystem access from here). `DecisionFile` takes
19	an `Executor` at construction and issues every read/write as a shell command through
20	it, so the SAME code path serves both roles; there is no separate "local write"
21	branch to accidentally use for the target.

24	`config.yaml` (D-09) — one file per manager, so `apt_sync`'s decisions never collide

233	        than aborting the sync; only the malformed case logs a WARNING (naming the
234	        path) since that one indicates the file was tampered with or hand-edited
235	        incorrectly, not simply "nothing recorded yet".
236	        """
237	        result = await self._executor.run_command(f"cat {self._path_expr} 2>/dev/null")

246	                self._display_path,

253	        atomically: `mkdir --parents` the directory, write the new content to a sibling

255	        atomic-replace-within-the-same-directory shape `vscode_state_sync._sync_editor`
256	        uses, so an interrupted write can never leave a truncated file.
257	
258	        The serialised bytes travel as one shlex-quoted `printf` argument through
259	        `self._executor` — never a local filesystem write — so this identical method
260	        is correct whether `self._executor` is the source's `LocalExecutor` or the
261	        target's `RemoteExecutor`.
262	        """
263	        entries = await self.load()
264	        entries[entry.item_id] = entry
265	        content = _serialize(entries)
266	
267	        dir_relpath = shlex.quote(_DECISION_DIR_RELPATH)
268	        tmp_expr = f"{self._path_expr}.pcswitcher-tmp"
269	        cmd = (
270	            f"mkdir --parents ~/{dir_relpath} && "
271	            f"printf '%s' {shlex.quote(content)} > {tmp_expr} && "
272	            f"mv --force {tmp_expr} {self._path_expr}"
273	        )
274	        result = await self._executor.run_command(
275	            cmd, mutates=f"record permanent skip for {entry.label} in {self._display_path}"
276	        )
277	        if not result.success:

279	                f"failed to record decision for {entry.item_id!r} in {self._display_path}: {result.stderr.strip()}"

288	    "# pc-switcher install-snippet registry — regenerated on every write.\n"
289	    "#\n"

293	    "# edit or remove an entry by hand if it goes stale.\n"
294	    "#\n"
295	    "# This file lives in the shared, synced config (D-23): every peer that runs\n"
296	    "# `pc-switcher sync` carries it to the target alongside config.yaml. A snippet\n"
297	    "# replays non-interactively with no stdin available — one that expects a prompt\n"
298	    "# fails rather than hanging the sync.\n"

302	@dataclass(frozen=True)
303	class Snippet:
304	    """One recorded install snippet (D-20): an opaque shell command that reproduces an
305	    item no package manager can install on its own.
306	
307	    `label` mirrors the unreproducible item's own label at authoring time (a snapshot,
308	    not a live reference) so the registry file reads meaningfully on its own. `body` is
309	    NEVER inspected by this dataclass or its callers beyond being replayed byte-for-byte:
310	    it arrives already stripped of surrounding whitespace from the one place a snippet is
311	    captured (`packages.review`), which is what keeps the YAML a person can read and the
312	    string `replay` quotes identical.
313	    """

315	    item_id: str
316	    label: str
317	    body: str
318	    authored_at: str  # ISO-8601 UTC
319	    authored_on: str  # hostname of the machine the snippet was authored on
320

322	def _serialize_snippets(entries: Mapping[str, Snippet]) -> str:
323	    """Render `entries` as the snippet-registry YAML body, header regenerated fresh."""
324	    snippets = {
325	        item_id: {
326	            "label": entry.label,
327	            "body": entry.body,
328	            "authored_at": entry.authored_at,
329	            "authored_on": entry.authored_on,
330	        }
331	        for item_id, entry in entries.items()
332	    }

337	#: Everything `yaml.safe_load` and the shape check below can throw for a file that is not
338	#: a snippet registry. Named once so the two entry points that read a registry — the
339	#: executor-backed `SnippetRegistry.load` and the on-disk `load_snippets_from_text` — cannot

341	_UNREADABLE = (yaml.YAMLError, KeyError, TypeError, ValueError, AttributeError)
342	
343	
344	def _unreadable_registry(display_path: str, machine: str | None, exc: Exception) -> SyncAborted:
345	    """The abort a registry that cannot be parsed raises (`PKG-FR-REGISTRY-CONSENT`).
346	
347	    An absent or empty registry means "no snippets"; a file that is there and cannot be read
348	    means nothing, and reading it as "no snippets" is what would let a wholesale push
349	    silently discard every entry the other machine holds. The run ends instead of the job
350	    failing, because the repair is a hand edit on one machine and the next sync is what
351	    should see the result — the same reason declining the overwrite question ends the run.
352	
353	    Plain `SyncAborted`, not the ByUser subclass: nobody was asked anything here, so
354	    nothing rendered from it may report the user as having stopped the sync (#224).
355	    """

359	        "repair or delete that file, then start a new sync"

362	
363	def _deserialize_snippets(raw: str) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
364	    """Parse a snippet registry's content into `{item_id: Snippet}`.
365	
366	    Raises anything in `_UNREADABLE` for content that is not a snippet registry; both
367	    callers turn that into `_unreadable_registry`'s abort.
368	
369	    Every entry is tried before that is raised, and the failure names all of them: the repair
370	    is a hand edit of this one file, and stopping at the first malformed entry would have the
371	    user fix it, start a new sync, and only then be shown the next.
372	    """
373	    data = yaml.safe_load(raw)
374	    snippets = data.get("snippets") if isinstance(data, dict) else None
375	    if not isinstance(snippets, dict):
376	        raise ValueError("snippet registry has no 'snippets' mapping")
377	
378	    entries: dict[str, Snippet] = {}
379	    malformed: list[str] = []
380	    for item_id, fields in snippets.items():
381	        try:
382	            entries[str(item_id)] = Snippet(
383	                item_id=str(item_id),
384	                label=fields["label"],
385	                body=fields["body"],
386	                authored_at=fields["authored_at"],
387	                authored_on=fields["authored_on"],
388	            )
389	        except KeyError as exc:
390	            malformed.append(f"{item_id} (missing field {exc})")
391	        except TypeError as exc:
392	            # The entry is not a mapping at all: a bare scalar, a list, or nothing.
393	            malformed.append(f"{item_id} ({exc})")
394	    if malformed:
395	        raise ValueError(f"unreadable snippet entries: {'; '.join(malformed)}")
396	    return entries
397	
398	
399	def load_snippets_from_text(raw: str, *, display_path: str, machine: str | None = None) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
400	    """Parse snippet-registry file content into `{item_id: Snippet}`; empty content means
401	    "no snippets" and content that cannot be parsed ends the run (`_unreadable_registry`) —
402	    the same rule `SnippetRegistry.load` applies to executor-read content.
403	
404	    `manual_installs_sync` uses this to read the SOURCE's on-disk registry — the exact
405	    bytes `_push_snippet_registry` is about to `send_file` to the target — when deciding
406	    whether a wholesale overwrite is purely additive (decision 9). Reading the file that
407	    is actually sent keeps the additive check consistent with the transfer, rather than
408	    re-querying the source executor which may lag the just-finalized on-disk file.
409	
410	    `display_path` and `machine` are what the abort names, since the raw text carries
411	    neither.
412	    """
413	    if not raw.strip():
414	        return {}
415	    try:
416	        return _deserialize_snippets(raw)
417	    except _UNREADABLE as exc:
418	        raise _unreadable_registry(display_path, machine, exc) from exc
419	
420	
421	class SnippetRegistry:
422	    """Read/write/replay access to the shared install-snippet registry, through
423	    whichever `Executor` is local to the machine this instance should read/write
424	    (same one-`Executor`-per-instance shape `DecisionFile` follows).
425	
426	    Unlike `DecisionFile`, the registry is not machine-scoped data — both machines may
427	    hold different copies of the SAME file until `manual_installs_sync` reconciles them
428	    by pushing the source's copy to the target (D-23). Construct with
429	    `SnippetRegistry(self.source)` to read/write the source's own copy — the reproducibility
430	    authority `plan()` classifies against (corrected D-23), and where a freshly authored
431	    snippet is recorded before that run's push carries it to the target — or
432	    `SnippetRegistry(self.target)` to read the target's copy at converge time, after this
433	    run's push has already placed it there.
434	    """
435	
436	    def __init__(self, executor: Executor, machine: str | None = None) -> None:
437	        self._executor = executor
438	        # The hostname of the machine this instance reads and writes, for the one message
439	        # that has to say WHICH copy of a same-named file is the problem. Optional so a
440	        # caller with no hostname to hand still gets a message naming the path.
441	        self._machine = machine
442	        # shlex.quote() is a no-op for this fixed, already-shell-safe relpath, applied
443	        # anyway per T-02-01 (ASVS V5) — see `DecisionFile.__init__`'s identical
444	        # reasoning for why it stays OUTSIDE the `~/` prefix.
445	        self._path_expr = f"~/{shlex.quote(SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH)}"
446	        self._display_path = f"~/{SNIPPET_REGISTRY_RELPATH}"
447	
448	    async def load(self) -> dict[str, Snippet]:
449	        """Read every snippet, or an empty mapping if the registry is absent or empty.
450	
451	        A registry that is THERE and cannot be parsed is neither: it ends the whole run
452	        (`_unreadable_registry`), because "no snippets" is a claim about the machine that
453	        this file no longer supports, and acting on it would push over entries nobody can
454	        see. Unlike `DecisionFile.load`, which degrades — a decision file that cannot be
455	        read costs the user a question they answered before, not their snippets.
456	        """
457	        result = await self._executor.run_command(f"cat {self._path_expr} 2>/dev/null")
458	        if not result.success or not result.stdout.strip():
459	            return {}
460	
461	        try:
462	            return _deserialize_snippets(result.stdout)
463	        except _UNREADABLE as exc:
464	            raise _unreadable_registry(self._display_path, self._machine, exc) from exc
465	
466	    async def get(self, item_id: str) -> Snippet | None:
467	        """The snippet registered for `item_id`, or `None` if there is none."""
468	        entries = await self.load()
469	        return entries.get(item_id)
470	
471	    async def add(self, snippet: Snippet) -> None:
472	        """Merge `snippet` into the registry by `item_id` (last write wins) and write
473	        atomically — the identical `mkdir --parents && printf ... > tmp && mv --force` shape
474	        `DecisionFile.record` uses, so an interrupted write can never leave a truncated
475	        file.
476	        """
477	        entries = await self.load()
478	        entries[snippet.item_id] = snippet
479	        content = _serialize_snippets(entries)
480	
481	        dir_relpath = shlex.quote(_DECISION_DIR_RELPATH)
482	        tmp_expr = f"{self._path_expr}.pcswitcher-tmp"
483	        cmd = (
484	            f"mkdir --parents ~/{dir_relpath} && "
485	            f"printf '%s' {shlex.quote(content)} > {tmp_expr} && "
486	            f"mv --force {tmp_expr} {self._path_expr}"
487	        )
488	        result = await self._executor.run_command(
489	            cmd, mutates=f"record install snippet for {snippet.label} in {self._display_path}"
490	        )
491	        if not result.success:
492	            raise RuntimeError(
493	                f"failed to add snippet for {snippet.item_id!r} in {self._display_path}: {result.stderr.strip()}"
494	            )
495	
496	    async def replay(self, item_id: str, executor: RemoteExecutor) -> CommandResult:
497	        """Replay the snippet registered for `item_id` against `executor` (always the
498	        TARGET in practice) as an opaque blob (D-20): the body is never parsed,
499	        templated or inspected, only quoted.
500	
501	        Runs as `bash -c <shlex.quote(body)>` — the same build-a-command,
502	        pass-content-as-an-argv-quoted-string shape `vscode_state_sync.target_sql_command`
503	        uses for SQL — with `login_shell=False`, since a snippet is a fixed shell script,
504	        not something that needs the user's `~/.profile` sourced. No stdin is ever
505	        supplied (`pcswitcher.executor.Process` documents this is intentional), so a
506	        snippet expecting a prompt fails rather than hanging the sync. The returned
507	        `CommandResult`'s exit code alone decides success — never raises for "no
508	        snippet registered", instead returning a failed `CommandResult` so a stale plan
509	        (the registry changed between `plan()` and `apply()`) is a per-item failure
510	        like any other, not a crash that stops the whole job (D-27).
511	
512	        The exact `bash -c <quoted body>` command is what `--confirm-each-command` shows:
513	        an opaque snippet is the one thing in a sync whose content pc-switcher cannot vouch
514	        for, so it is displayed verbatim before it runs.
515	        """
516	        snippet = await self.get(item_id)
517	        if snippet is None:
518	            return CommandResult(exit_code=1, stdout="", stderr=f"no snippet registered for {item_id!r}")
519	
520	        cmd = f"bash -c {shlex.quote(snippet.body)}"
521	        return await executor.run_command(
522	            cmd, login_shell=False, mutates=f"replay install snippet for {snippet.label}"
523	        )

## 5. What to check while answering

The jobs run in order — apt, snap, flatpak, manual, then the folder mirror — and each one's questions come before the next one plans. The mirror asks nothing and runs last, which is what lets it read from pc2 what the package jobs left there.

- Use a shifted key on one multi-item group first, to confirm it sets every line, then correct the lines you did not mean.
- Each group is one question: every item on a line, the answer it carries in a column to the right, arrows moving between lines, `<space>` cycling the focused line, `<enter>` confirming. Nothing is asked a second time.
- The legend's permanent answer reads `keep on pc2 for good; it is pc2's own, and will not be asked again` on a removal and `do not install on pc2 for good; it is pc1's own, and will not be asked again` on an install; a question that records nothing is the same widget with `<x>` missing.
- `sl` is offered for install and nothing anywhere asks about its hold: a hold travels with its package, so no group, line or legend mentions one.
- The report group is titled `Version differences (apt packages)` and notes ``These converge on their own: run `sudo apt update && sudo apt upgrade` on pc2.``
- The collateral question is titled `Removing fortunes-min on pc2 would remove fortunes`, and the line under that title — above the keys, not under the row — says it is protected on both grounds, naming `pc2` as the machine the mark is on. It names `fortunes` and offers three answers on one row: the act `<y>`, hinted `remove fortunes-min from pc2, so fortunes is removed as well`; `skip now` `<s>`; and `stop the sync` `<q>`, hinted `nothing more is changed on pc2; what earlier jobs already did stays done`. There is no `<x>`.
- Only after those screens are confirmed does `Delete apt repositories pc1 no longer has` appear — a second round, asked because of the answers you just gave. It comes one file at a time and offers `99-pcsw-uat.sources` only, its detail reading `pc2 would stop getting software from https://***@packages.example.com/apt` — the password appears nowhere. `99-pcsw-inuse.sources` is not asked about at all.
- `snap_sync` asks two questions, install before change — the order every job puts its groups in. `Install snap packages` offers `hello-world (latest/stable, revision <pc1's>)` and nothing else, with the ordinary three answers and its row starting at install: pc2 lost it in §2 and this question is what brings it back. Leave it applied.
- `Align snap package versions` follows, with two answers and no `<x>`, its act reading `align`: `hello`'s line reads `overwrites revision <pc2's> on pc2 with revision <pc1's> from pc1`, and the row starts applied rather than skipped.
- `flatpak_sync` asks once, `Install flatpak applications`, offering `io.github.fragglet.sdl_sopwith/x86_64/stable (2.9.0, flathub, user)` and nothing else, with the ordinary three answers and its row starting at install; leave it applied. Nothing else in that job is a question: the runtime the application needs travels with it, and no remote is ever offered — neither pc1's `flathub-beta` nor the deletion of pc2's `pcsw-uat`, which the log records instead (§6).
- `manual_installs_sync` asks `What is /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor on pc1?` while it is still planning, before its review: it names `alpha` and `beta`, and its two answers say what pc2 would be given either way.
- Its review then offers `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor`, in that order, and nothing else — `/opt/pcsw-uat-empty`, `/usr/local/share/pcsw-uat-note` and `/usr/local/bin/pcsw-uat` are named nowhere, the last of them because pc2 already has it. Each item is asked on its own with three answers, titled `Install /opt/pcsw-uat-app on pc2?` and `Install /opt/pcsw-uat-vendor on pc2?`, and answering `<y>` opens the editor saying `(Ctrl-D to finish)`. Submit an empty body, then one of only spaces: each must be refused and the three answers offered again.
- Ctrl-C on any group ends the whole sync with `package review aborted at '<that group's title>' (Ctrl-C)`, exit code 1, and a terminal that still works.

## 6. What to check afterwards

On pc1:

```bash
grep -c cmatrix ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml       # 1 — an install is recorded here
grep -c cowsay ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml        # 0
grep -c pcsw-uat-vendor ~/.config/pc-switcher/manual.decisions.yaml  # 1 — pc1 holds it, so pc1 records it
grep -c pcsw-uat-app ~/.config/pc-switcher/package-snippets.yaml     # 1 — the snippet you wrote
LOG=$(ls -t ~/.local/share/pc-switcher/logs/sync-*.log | head -1)
grep -E 'reviewed cowsay|reviewed fortunes \(report_only\)' "$LOG"   # "marked as this machine's own", then "applied"
grep -n -E 'apt-get.*sl=|apt-mark hold sl' "$LOG"              # pc1's exact version, then the hold, in that order
grep -E 'keeping repository 99-pcsw-inuse.sources' "$LOG"
grep -n -E 'apply the ref filter /home/testuser/uat.filter|sdl_sopwith' "$LOG" | head
grep -E 'delete user flatpak remote pcsw-uat' "$LOG"
grep -c "s3c'ret" "$LOG"                                       # 0
grep -c 'stdout: ' "$LOG"                                      # apt's, snap's and flatpak's own output, verbatim
grep -c 'send_file.*package-snippets.yaml' "$LOG"              # 1 — the job's own push, the registry's only route
```

The filter line must come before any `sdl_sopwith` install: the filter is in force before anything installs from that remote, and pc2's own filter is never taken off for the install's benefit.

On pc2:

```bash
grep -c cowsay ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml    # 1 — a removal is recorded here
grep -c cmatrix ~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml   # 0
dpkg-query -W -f='${Package} ${Version} ${Status}\n' sl cmatrix fortunes fortunes-min
apt-mark showhold                                # sl, registered after its install landed
snap list hello hello-world                      # hello at pc1's revision, hello-world arrived
flatpak remotes --user --columns=name,filter     # flathub carries uat.filter, pcsw-uat is gone
flatpak list --user --app --columns=application  # sopwith arrived under pc1's filter
ls /etc/apt/sources.list.d/ /opt /opt/pcsw-uat-app
ls ~/snap/hello                                  # pc1's revision and current, and no second revision directory
```

`sl` is installed at pc1's version and `cmatrix` is absent; `fortunes` and `fortunes-min` are both gone, the collateral answer having taken them; both `.sources` files are still there; `/opt/pcsw-uat-app` exists with its `README`, the snippet having replayed in the run that authored it, and `/opt/pcsw-uat-vendor` does not — it is pc1's own.

The mirror ran over `/home` after all four package jobs, and what it left is the boundary: `uat-converged` is on pc2 because pc2's own snapd ends the run on that revision, and `uat-stray` is not, because the revision it holds data for is the one this run moved pc2 off. The two `apt.decisions.yaml` checks above are the same boundary read from the other side — each machine still holds its own record, so the mirror carried neither machine's decision file to the other.

## 7. Two runs with no terminal

`ssh` without `-t` leaves the run no terminal, which is the only way to reach these paths. Sideload `hello-world` on pc2 first: a sideloaded snap is out of scope on both machines, so the run must neither move it nor mention it.

"""Item model shared by every package job (D-02, ADR-020).

Item identity is the primary key for the whole subsystem: every package, apt source,
signing key, pin, config file, snap, snap channel, flatpak ref, flatpak remote and
unreproducible install this phase handles is identified by a stable `item_id` string,
not by any manager-specific value. A package name, a flatpak ref, a filename — each is
a FIELD of one variant's dataclass, never the primary key itself. This is what lets the
review and decision-file pipeline operate on one shape (`ItemDiff`) regardless of which
manager produced it.

What belongs here is only what more than one manager uses. A shape only `snap_sync`
constructs lives in `snap_sync`; `AptSourceItem` lives in `apt_sync`; a detail string
only `flatpak_sync` writes lives in `flatpak_sync`. The four jobs are deliberately
independent (D-15), and a registry of everyone's private shapes is a shared surface
they have to agree on — it couples the jobs without any of them gaining a thing.

`ItemClass` and `DiffClass` stay whole here even though each member is produced by one
manager: they are the taxonomy the shared review and the decision files are keyed on, so
they are the definition of what the pipeline can carry, not one manager's business.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass
from enum import StrEnum

from pcswitcher.redaction import redact_credentials

__all__ = [
    "DiffAction",
    "DiffClass",
    "ItemClass",
    "ItemDiff",
    "Machines",
    "build_version_mismatch_detail",
]


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Machines:
    """The two machines' own names, for every string a user reads.

    Source and target are ROLES this run assigns; they are not what the user calls the two
    computers in front of them, and a review line that says "the target" makes the reader
    translate before they can decide. Carried as one value rather than two parameters because
    every detail builder that needs one usually needs both, and because a builder that takes
    it is built once per job from `JobContext`, so no call site can pair the two names up
    itself and get them the wrong way round.
    """

    source: str
    target: str


class ItemClass(StrEnum):
    """The full D-02 item-class taxonomy.

    Not every member is reviewable in every direction. `APT_SOURCE` and `APT_PIN` identify
    reviewed REMOVALS only, and `FLATPAK_REMOTE` likewise: adds and changes for all three
    are derived from the packages or refs approved from them (ADR-020 D-34/D-36/D-41) and
    carry no `item_id` at all. `SNAP_CHANNEL` never becomes a standalone item; see
    `SnapItem`'s docstring. A signing key has no member here in any direction.
    """

    APT_PACKAGE = "apt_package"
    APT_SOURCE = "apt_source"
    APT_PIN = "apt_pin"
    APT_CONFIG = "apt_config"
    APT_HOLD = "apt_hold"
    SNAP = "snap"
    SNAP_CHANNEL = "snap_channel"
    SNAP_HOLD = "snap_hold"

class DiffClass(StrEnum):
    """The full D-25 conflict taxonomy. Each manager's own diff decides which members it
    can produce; the enum is the definition of what the shared review and the decision
    files can carry, not one manager's business.

    `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` and `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` are the two provenance members (ADR-020 D-34)
    and are about WHERE an item comes from, not whether it is present:

    - `REPO_UNAVAILABLE` — the source's origin cannot be provided on the target, so the
      item is reported rather than installed from somewhere else. It is a statement about
      provenance, NOT "apt printed `Candidate: (none)`" — that says nothing about where a
      package comes from and reads as unavailable for packages the target could install.
    - `ORIGIN_MISMATCH` — present on both machines, from two different vendors. A real
      divergence a presence-and-version diff cannot see.

    There is deliberately no `HELD_OR_PINNED` member. A hold replicates as its own
    `apt:hold:`/`snap:hold:` membership item, and a pin's only effect — which origin wins —
    is read back off the target after the refresh (ADR-020 D-35) rather than echoed onto
    every package a pin file happens to name. Such an echo makes a target-only package
    named by any pin impossible to remove: `REPORT_ONLY` outranks its own
    `EXTRA_ON_TARGET`/`REMOVE` diff, and a report-only item cannot be skipped-always
    either.
    """

    MISSING_ON_TARGET = "missing_on_target"
    EXTRA_ON_TARGET = "extra_on_target"
    VERSION_MISMATCH = "version_mismatch"
    REPO_UNAVAILABLE = "repo_unavailable"
    ORIGIN_MISMATCH = "origin_mismatch"
    UNREPRODUCIBLE = "unreproducible"


class DiffAction(StrEnum):
    """The concrete converge verb a diff implies (D-07's direction-dependent "apply").

    Values match `packages.review`'s private removal-action set (`{"remove", "delete",
    "disable"}`) so a `ReviewGroup` built from these actions gets the right
    default-checked/unchecked behavior without that module knowing this enum exists.
    """

    INSTALL = "install"
    REMOVE = "remove"

=== requirements section ===
## Decisions and their memory: "machine specific"

**Apply** does the thing. **Skip** declines it for this run only. **Always skip** marks the item as **machine-specific**. The mark is recorded on the **holding machine** — not necessarily the machine the sync was launched from.

Example: two machines Atlas and Vega, sync launched from Atlas. Vega has `steam`; Atlas does not, so the sync offers to remove it from Vega. Answering "always skip" writes the mark **on Vega**, because Vega holds `steam`. The reverse case: Atlas has `wireshark`, the sync offers to install it on Vega, and "always skip" writes the mark on **Atlas**.

A machine-specific item is filtered out before the difference is computed, so it never appears in a later review. Because of that, the repository-conflict question below has to disclose it explicitly.

Marks never sync between machines. Snippets do, because how to install something is knowledge about the software rather than the machine.

Repositories and pins cannot be marked machine-specific, whether they are being added, changed or deleted; a flatpak remote is never asked about at all, so there is nothing to mark. Where the two machines disagree about where software comes from, that disagreement keeps surfacing every run instead of being silenced once, and the remedy is to align the two machines. apt's own configuration files *can* be marked, because they say how apt behaves rather than where software comes from.

Blocks cannot be marked either. A hold and a mask are never asked about at all, so there is nothing to mark, and a mark on the software they apply to silences them with it.

A snap's revision or channel cannot be marked. Nobody holds a revision as a standing preference about one machine, and a mark would leave the two machines' manifests disagreeing about a snap neither would raise again; skipping it for the run says what the user means, and the difference surfaces again next sync.

Report-only findings cannot be marked either — no machine holds a version difference, and a mark would stop the package syncing rather than stop the report.

## Symptom

UAT 02-01 §4/§6: pc2 records `apt:package:fortunes` machine-specific, the collateral answer then removes `fortunes-min` **and `fortunes`** from pc2, and pc2's `~/.config/pc-switcher/apt.decisions.yaml` still holds the `fortunes` entry afterwards. A mark for software the machine no longer has.

`DecisionFile` (`src/pcswitcher/jobs/packages/state.py:206-280`) exposes only `load` and `record`. No code path anywhere removes an entry, so this is not specific to collateral — a mark is written once and lives forever.

## Why it is wrong

Beyond the file accumulating dead entries, a stale mark keeps acting. `filter_inert` drops the item before any diff is computed, in **both** roles, on **both** machines' files (`marks_on_either`). So once pc2 has lost `fortunes`, a later sync from a machine that has `fortunes` will silently not offer to install it on pc2 — the user is never asked and never told.

That inverts the answer they gave. "Always skip" on a **removal** means *keep my copy*; it does not mean *never install this here*. When the copy it was protecting is gone, the mark has outlived the statement it recorded.

## Where else this happens

Any way the holding machine can lose a marked item, not just collateral:

- collateral removal takes a marked package (the UAT case)
- the user removes/uninstalls a marked package, snap or flatpak ref by hand
- a marked `apt:config:` file or a marked unowned path under `/opt`/`/usr/local` is deleted by hand
- a marked item is lost to a reinstall, a distro upgrade, or a restore from backup

## The invariant that makes this fixable

`PKG-FR-MACHINE-SPECIFIC` + D-08a: a mark is always recorded on the machine that **holds** the item — install → source, removal → target, change → the machine whose copy is kept (both machines have it). In every case the item is present on the machine whose file carries the mark.

So: **item absent from the holding machine ⇒ the mark is dead.** That is a local check on one machine against one file, with no cross-machine reasoning.

## Proposed solution

Two parts, one rule.

### A. Same-run drop

When a job's converge removes or deletes an item, it drops that item's mark from the holding machine's file in the same run — including collateral casualties, which the apt job already tracks by name (`Collateral.protected`/`approved_removals`, `jobs/apt_sync/collateral.py`). This is what fixes the UAT case at the moment it arises rather than one sync later.

### B. Next-run reconcile

At plan time, each package job compares its own manager's decision entries — on **both** machines, since either end can be a holder — against a positive existence check on the machine holding the file, and drops entries whose item is gone. This covers every out-of-band disappearance, and running it at plan time means the diff for that run is already computed against a live mark set.

Existence oracle per markable item class (all cheap, all on the holding machine):

| item_id prefix | present means |
| --- | --- |
| `apt:package:` | `dpkg-query` reports `install ok installed` |
| `apt:config:` | the file exists under `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d/` |
| `snap:` | `snap list <name>` succeeds |
| `flatpak:ref:<scope>:` | the ref is in `flatpak list --<scope>` |
| `unreproducible:unowned-path:` | the path exists |
| `unreproducible:apt-no-candidate:` | the package is installed |

### Guard rails

- **Positive absence only.** Prune on an existence check that ran and said "not there" — never on absence from a derived set. `apt-mark showmanual` is the trap: a package that flips to auto-installed leaves that set while still installed, and pruning off it would drop a live mark.
- **Failed or partial capture prunes nothing.** A command that did not succeed means "unknown", not "gone".
- **Only classes the running job owns.** A run with `snap_sync` disabled must not touch `snap.decisions.yaml`; an entry of a class that cannot be marked at all (`apt:hold:`, `apt:source:`, `apt:pin:`, `flatpak:remote:`, `flatpak:mask:`, `snap:hold:`) — reachable only by hand-editing — is left alone rather than guessed at.
- **Never silent.** Each drop logs at INFO naming the item and that the machine no longer has it. Marks are the one thing in the subsystem the user is promised is durable; them vanishing has to be readable in the log.
- `DecisionFile` needs a write path that removes entries (`drop(item_ids)` / rewrite), atomic and `mutates=`-gated like `record`.

### Behaviour this settles

If the item reappears on that machine later, it is reviewed again as a new item. That is the intended reading — the earlier answer was about the copy that is gone — but it is a change to "MUST NOT be proposed in any later review" and has to be written down, not left implied.

## Rejected alternatives

- **Age-based expiry of marks.** Age says nothing about whether the item is still there.
- **Keep stale marks, only report them.** Leaves the silent-suppression bug in place; the user has to hand-edit YAML to fix something the tool can see.
- **Prune only in the collateral path.** Fixes the one case in the runbook and none of the others.

## Also needs updating

- `docs/planning/package-sync-conformance-criteria.md` — `PKG-FR-MACHINE-SPECIFIC` gains the lifetime rule
- `docs/planning/package-sync-user-requirements.md` — "Decisions and their memory" section
- ADR-020 — a decision entry for mark lifetime, alongside D-08/D-08a
- `docs/dev/package-sync-scenario-coverage.md` — H.10, plus a scenario per disappearance route
- `.planning/phases/02-package-management-sync/02-UAT-01-RUNBOOK.md` §6 — pc2 check that the `fortunes` mark is gone, not just the package

Issue: https://github.com/flaksit/pc-switcher/issues/242 (`type:bug`, `comp:sync:packages`, `ai:needs-speckit`, `P1`)

**The general defect**, not just the `fortunes` case: `DecisionFile` (`packages/state.py:206-280`) exposes only `load` and `record` — nothing anywhere removes an entry, so a mark written once lives forever regardless of what happens to the item.

**Why it's more than untidy state**: `filter_inert` drops marked items before any diff, in both roles, reading both machines' files. Once pc2 lost `fortunes`, a later sync from a machine that has it will silently not offer to install it on pc2. That inverts the answer — "always skip" on a *removal* means "keep my copy", not "never install here".

**The invariant the fix rests on** (D-08a): a mark always sits on the machine that *holds* the item — install→source, removal→target, change→the machine whose copy is kept, which also has it. So *item absent from the holding machine ⇒ mark is dead*, checkable locally per file.

**Proposal**, two parts:
- Same-run drop — a job's converge that removes an item drops its mark then and there, collateral casualties included (apt already tracks those by name in `Collateral`). Fixes the UAT case at the moment it arises.
- Next-run reconcile at plan time — each job checks its manager's entries on both machines against a per-class existence oracle (dpkg installed / file exists / `snap list` / `flatpak list` / path exists) and drops the dead ones.

Guard rails matter more than the mechanism: prune only on a *positive* absence from a check that succeeded — never on absence from a derived set (`apt-mark showmanual` is the trap: a package flipping to auto leaves that set while still installed); a failed capture prunes nothing; jobs touch only their own manager's file and only classes that can be marked; every drop logs.

The one behavioural decision to confirm: a pruned item that reappears gets reviewed again as new. I think that's right — the earlier answer was about the copy that's gone — but it's a change to "MUST NOT be proposed in any later review", so the issue lists the requirement, ADR-020, coverage-matrix and runbook updates it implies rather than treating it as implied.

292	    @abstractmethod
293	    async def plan(self) -> PackagePlan:
294	        """Capture, diff and build this job's review groups. Read-only.
295	
296	        Every manager owns its own: what a diff even IS differs per ecosystem (apt has
297	        pins, holds and transaction collateral; snap converges a revision and a channel;
298	        flatpak carries scope and remote trust; a manual install has a snippet or has
299	        nothing). There is no diff shape all four share, so there is no base
300	        implementation to inherit — only the pieces below, which every implementation
301	        does use: `filter_inert` on the way in, `_drop_inert_diffs` on the way out, and
302	        `_build_review_groups` at the end.
303	
304	        Nothing here may mutate either machine: a job plans and reviews before it
305	        converges, so `plan()` runs before the user has approved anything. An
306	        implementation MUST load both machines' decision files and filter each side's
307	        items through its OWN file (D-08), then run the resulting diffs through
308	        `_drop_inert_diffs` to catch the recorded items no input-side filter can see —
309	        the block-state membership items (`apt:hold:`, `snap:hold:`) and anything else
310	        whose identity is derived rather than carried on an input item.
311	        """
312	        ...
313	
314	    @abstractmethod
315	    async def converge(self, diff: ItemDiff) -> CommandResult:
316	        """Apply one approved diff on the target.
317	
318	        May raise `ConvergeItemFailed` to refuse the item without even attempting the
319	        mutating command (e.g. a transaction-safety guard), or `ConvergeItemDeclined` for
320	        one the user withdrew after the review; otherwise returns the
321	        `CommandResult` of the converge command, whose `.success` decides pass/fail.
322	        Called for every APPLY-decided diff whose action is `INSTALL`, `REMOVE` or
323	        `CHANGE` — `REPORT_ONLY` diffs never reach this hook (see `apply()`).
324	        """
325	        ...
326	
327	    @property
328	    def machines(self) -> Machines:
329	        """The two machines' own names, for every string this job puts in front of the user."""
330	        return Machines(source=self.context.source_hostname, target=self.context.target_hostname)

332	    @staticmethod
333	    def _mark_holders(action: DiffAction) -> tuple[bool, ...]:
334	        """The machines a machine-specific mark on a diff of this action can sit on, as
335	        "is it the source" flags, THE RECORDING MACHINE FIRST (D-08a,
336	        `PKG-FR-MACHINE-SPECIFIC`).
337	
338	        One definition serving both halves, and the ordering is what makes them agree by
339	        construction: the WRITE path (`_record_permanent_skips`) takes the first flag to
340	        pick the executor whose file gets the entry, and the READ path
341	        (`_drop_inert_diffs`) looks in every file the tuple names, which always includes
342	        the one the write used.
343	
344	        The holding machine is "the one whose state the mark describes", and the action
345	        states which machines have the item at all:
346	
347	        - `INSTALL` — only the source has it, so only the source can describe it.
348	        - `REMOVE` — only the target has it.
349	        - `CHANGE` — BOTH have it, with different content, and the answer keeps the
350	          TARGET's copy: what the user refused permanently is the overwrite of the machine
351	          they are syncing TO, which is the machine the review names in the same words
352	          ("it is <target>'s own", `review._hints`). But which machine that was depends on
353	          the direction the run that recorded the mark was launched in, and the direction
354	          of a later run says nothing about it — so a change is read back from either
355	          machine's file. Reading only one of them makes the mark hold in the direction it
356	          was given and evaporate in the other.
357	        """
358	        if action is DiffAction.CHANGE:
359	            return (False, True)
360	        return (action is DiffAction.INSTALL,)

362	    def _drop_inert_diffs(
363	        self,
364	        diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff],
365	        source_decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry],
366	        target_decisions: Mapping[str, DecisionEntry],
367	    ) -> tuple[ItemDiff, ...]:
368	        """Drop every diff whose `item_id` is recorded "skip always" on a machine that could
369	        hold it (`_mark_holders`, D-08/D-08a) — the post-diff counterpart to `filter_inert`.
370	
371	        Required for any diff whose identity does not exist on an input item and so cannot
372	        be filtered at the diff-input boundary: the block-state membership items
373	        (`apt:hold:<name>`, `snap:hold:<name>`) are derived from hold-set membership, and
374	        apt's repo/collateral diffs are derived from directory digests. Without this pass
375	        a permanently-declined hold is re-emitted every run — and in the add direction it
376	        comes back default-checked, so a bulk accept applies the very hold the user
377	        declined.
378	
379	        Reading the holder off the ACTION is only correct while the action is a true
380	        statement of which machines have the item, which is why `filter_inert` drops a
381	        marked item from BOTH inventories rather than from its own machine's alone: a
382	        surviving copy on the other machine turns "no item" into a one-sided item pointing
383	        the wrong way, and this pass would then look the mark up in the wrong file.
384	
385	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs pass through untouched: they carry no converge verb, so
386	        `_record_permanent_skips` never records one and there is no holder to match. So do
387	        block diffs, in every direction: a block is derived and no answer about one can be
388	        recorded (`PKG-FR-BLOCKS-DERIVED`), so an entry naming one — left by an older
389	        version of the tool, or written by hand — must not silence a replication the user
390	        never declined. A mark on the SOFTWARE still reaches its blocks, in each manager's
391	        own diff, because that is a mark the user did give.
392	        """
393	        kept: list[ItemDiff] = []
394	        for diff in diffs:
395	            if diff.item_class in BLOCK_ITEM_CLASSES:
396	                kept.append(diff)
397	                continue
398	            if diff.action not in (DiffAction.INSTALL, DiffAction.CHANGE, DiffAction.REMOVE):
399	                kept.append(diff)
400	                continue
401	            holders = [
402	                source_decisions if is_source else target_decisions for is_source in self._mark_holders(diff.action)
403	            ]
404	            if not any(diff.item_id in holder for holder in holders):
405	                kept.append(diff)
406	        return tuple(kept)

408	    def _build_review_groups(self, diffs: Sequence[ItemDiff]) -> tuple[ReviewGroup, ...]:
409	        """One `ReviewGroup` per `(action, item_class)` present in `diffs`, keyed on
410	        `(manager, action)` for the reviewer's removal-direction test (D-24) so removals
411	        never share a group with installs. The title's verb and every entry's
412	        `action_label` come from `_ACTION_VOCABULARY`, keyed by the group's own item class.
413	        `_ITEM_CLASS_NOUN` does the same for the title's OBJECT, so the one reviewed class
414	        that is not a package — `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` — is not announced as one, and
415	        `_ACTION_CLASS_NOUN` overrides it where one action's group is about something
416	        narrower than the class itself (a snap CHANGE moves versions, not packages). Grouping by
417	        item class as well as action is what keeps that verb correct when one action mixes
418	        item classes; the group's `action` value is normally the raw `DiffAction`, so
419	        add-direction stays default-checked and remove-direction lands in its own unticked
420	        group. `_GROUP_ACTION` overrides it where a class must not be offered the permanent
421	        answer — a snap's revision or channel (`PKG-FR-NO-MARK-ON-SNAP-REVISION`), whose
422	        group action is a sentinel the reviewer's promotable set does not contain.
423	
424	        Emission order: `_ACTION_ORDER` (install, change, remove, report) outer, and
425	        within one action the item classes in first-seen order.
426	
427	        Blocks are absent from every group, whichever direction they are in
428	        (`PKG-FR-BLOCKS-DERIVED`): a hold and a mask replicate because the software they
429	        apply to does, exactly as a pin does, so there is nothing here for the user to
430	        answer. They stay in `PackagePlan.diffs`, where `accept_review` gives them
431	        `Decision.APPLY` and `apply()` converges and reports them by name.
432	        """
433	        diffs = [diff for diff in diffs if diff.item_class not in BLOCK_ITEM_CLASSES]
434	
435	        # A reported condition is keyed by its CAUSE as well (ruled by the user): version
436	        # drift, an origin the target cannot reproduce and a package installed from two
437	        # different repositories were one group called "Report apt packages", which named
438	        # none of them. `DiffClass` is that cause, and report-only is the one action whose
439	        # members carry different ones.
440	        by_key: dict[tuple[DiffAction, ItemClass, DiffClass | None], list[ItemDiff]] = {}
441	        class_order: dict[DiffAction, list[tuple[ItemClass, DiffClass | None]]] = {}
442	        for diff in diffs:
443	            cause = diff.diff_class if diff.action is DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else None
444	            key = (diff.action, diff.item_class, cause)
445	            if key not in by_key:
446	                by_key[key] = []
447	                class_order.setdefault(diff.action, []).append((diff.item_class, cause))
448	            by_key[key].append(diff)
449	
450	        groups: list[ReviewGroup] = []
451	        for action in _ACTION_ORDER:
452	            for item_class, cause in class_order.get(action, []):
453	                entries = by_key[(action, item_class, cause)]
454	                # REPORT_ONLY has no more-specific per-item-class meaning for any current
455	                # manager (IN-01): fall back to "report" rather than the raw enum value
456	                # ("report_only"), which read awkwardly in review text like "Report_only
457	                # flatpak packages". Every other action still falls back to its own
458	                # `action.value`, unchanged.
459	                default_verb = "report" if action == DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY else action.value
460	                verb = _ACTION_VOCABULARY.get((item_class, action), default_verb)
461	                default_noun = f"{self.manager_id} {_MANAGER_NOUN.get(self.manager_id, 'packages')}"
462	                noun = _ACTION_CLASS_NOUN.get((item_class, action)) or _ITEM_CLASS_NOUN.get(item_class, default_noun)
463	                title = f"{verb.capitalize()} {noun}"
464	                note = None
465	                if cause is not None:
466	                    cause_title = _REPORT_TITLES.get(cause, "Reported").format(
467	                        target=self.machines.target,
468	                        origins=_MANAGER_ORIGIN_NOUN.get(self.manager_id, "repositories"),
469	                    )
470	                    title = f"{cause_title} ({noun})"
471	                    # A manager with no upgrade command of its own gets no note rather than
472	                    # a sentence with a hole in it.
473	                    upgrade = _UPGRADE_COMMANDS.get(self.manager_id)
474	                    template = _REPORT_NOTES.get(cause)
475	                    if template and upgrade:
476	                        note = template.format(target=self.machines.target, upgrade=upgrade)
477	                groups.append(
478	                    ReviewGroup(
479	                        manager=self.manager_id,
480	                        action=_GROUP_ACTION.get((item_class, action), action.value),
481	                        title=title,
482	                        note=note or None,
483	                        # `PKG-FR-HARMLESS-DEFAULT`: an `/etc/apt/apt.conf.d` file the target
484	                        # already holds says how the user's own apt behaves there, so
485	                        # replacing it is an overwrite of their work and starts at skip-once.
486	                        # A snap moved to another revision or channel does not: converging
487	                        # software the user asked for overwrites nothing they authored.
488	                        overwrites_authored_content=item_class is ItemClass.APT_CONFIG and action is DiffAction.CHANGE,
489	                        entries=tuple(
490	                            ReviewEntry(
491	                                item_id=diff.item_id,
492	                                label=diff.label,
493	                                action_label=verb,
494	                                detail=diff.detail,
495	                            )
496	                            for diff in entries
497	                        ),
498	                    )
499	                )
500	        return tuple(groups)

504	    async def plan_second_round(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> PackagePlan:
505	        """Hook: the questions this job can only put once the first round's answers exist.
506	
507	        Returns the run's FINAL item set as `diffs` and the SECOND round's groups as
508	        `groups` — nothing on the base, since only `apt_sync` has such a question today.
509	        `execute()` puts those groups to the same reviewer immediately after the first round
510	        returns and merges the two answer sets, so both rounds precede every change this job
511	        makes (`PKG-FR-REVIEW-FIRST`, `PKG-FR-CONSENT-BEFORE-CHANGE`).
512	
513	        It exists because an article can scope its question to the work this run APPROVES,
514	        which is a fact no plan-time computation holds: `PKG-FR-REPO-CONFLICT` raises its
515	        question "only for a repository this run writes because an approved package comes
516	        from it", `PKG-FR-REPO-DELETE` counts a repository's users "after this run's approved
517	        removals" and forbids raising the item at all while any remain, and
518	        `PKG-FR-COLLATERAL-MARKED` requires a mark recorded earlier in the same run to count.
519	        Building every item before any answer exists is what made those three questions
520	        approximations of what their articles ask for.
521	
522	        `PKG-FR-BATCHED` is what licenses the second round: the questions still come one
523	        after another with no work between them — an implementation may issue READS here,
524	        never a change — and each recurring kind of decision is still settled in one pass.
525	        `PKG-FR-ASK-AGAIN` is a different permission for a different case, asking after the
526	        target has already been changed, which is `LateCollateral`'s round rather than this
527	        one.
528	        """
529	        return PackagePlan(manager=plan.manager, diffs=plan.diffs, groups=())

531	    def accept_review(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> None:
532	        """Store this job's plan plus the outcome its own review returned, with every block
533	        decided `APPLY` (`PKG-FR-BLOCKS-DERIVED`).
534	
535	        A block reached no review group, so the reviewer returned no answer for it, and the
536	        default for a missing answer is skip-once — which would silently drop the very
537	        replication the article requires without review. It is decided here rather than in
538	        `apply()` so every consumer of the accepted outcome sees the same thing: the converge
539	        loop and the dry-run preview alike.
540	
541	        This is not a decision about whether the block LANDS. A freeze block whose software
542	        this run did not put on the target is refused by its own manager's converger, which
543	        is the only place that knows whether the install ran (`PKG-FR-APT-HOLD-INERT`).
544	
545	        Deliberately after any subclass has finished rewriting the outcome (`apt_sync`'s
546	        collateral resolution downgrades an approved install to skip-once), so nothing here
547	        overwrites an answer the user gave about software.
548	        """
549	        blocks = [diff.item_id for diff in plan.diffs if diff.item_class in BLOCK_ITEM_CLASSES]
550	        if blocks:
551	            outcome = ReviewOutcome(
552	                decisions={**outcome.decisions, **dict.fromkeys(blocks, Decision.APPLY)},
553	                was_interactive=outcome.was_interactive,
554	                snippets=outcome.snippets,
555	                unresolved=outcome.unresolved,
556	            )
557	        self._accepted_plan = plan
558	        self._accepted_outcome = outcome

560	    async def after_review(self) -> None:
561	        """Hook: work that must run AFTER this job's review returns but BEFORE any
562	        mutation on the target (`apply()`). Called only when the review was interactive
563	        (`execute()`), since everything this seam exists for acts on an answer.
564	
565	        No-op on the base — the three managers that produce no unreproducible items (apt,
566	        snap, flatpak) need nothing between review and converge. Only `manual_installs_sync`
567	        overrides it (D-23): it pushes the freshly reconciled install-snippet registry to
568	        the target here, so a snippet the user authored during THIS run's review is on the
569	        target before `apply()` replays it. Keeping the hook on the base leaves `execute()`
570	        the single source of the plan/review/apply order rather than each manager
571	        re-deriving it.
572	        """
573	        return

575	    async def apply(self) -> None:
576	        """Converge every APPLY-decided diff from the accepted plan, one item at a time.
577	
578	        Per-item detail at `LogLevel.FULL`, one `LogLevel.INFO` summary line per job
579	        (ADR-010). Progress is reported BEFORE each item rather than after it, and carries
580	        that item's label: the UI creates a job's bar lazily on its first update, so a job
581	        applying a single long item used to show no bar at all while it ran (#235), and an
582	        anonymous bar could not say which item it was waiting on. The completed bar is the
583	        one report the loop makes after its last item.
584	
585	        A per-item failure (`ConvergeItemFailed`, or a converge command that
586	        exits non-zero) is caught, logged with its stderr as structured context, and
587	        collected — the loop always completes (D-27) — then `PackageItemFailures` is
588	        raised once, after the loop, if anything failed OR anything is left unresolved
589	        (D-21) — even when `total` is zero, since an interactive run whose ONLY diffs
590	        were unreproducible items never has any INSTALL/CHANGE/REMOVE work to do, and
591	        must still fail if one of them ended up unresolved.
592	
593	        `ConvergeItemDeclined` is the third outcome: the item is neither applied nor
594	        failed, because the user withdrew it after the review (`PKG-FR-ASK-AGAIN`). It is
595	        named in its own summary line so the run says what happened to it, and it never
596	        reaches `PackageItemFailures`.
597	
598	        Dry-run (ADR-014): each intended action is logged at FULL with a `[dry-run] `
599	        prefix, carrying the diff's own detail, and no converge command is ever issued.
600	
601	        `REPORT_ONLY` diffs are excluded here regardless of decision: they imply no
602	        converge verb (D-25's version-mismatch, repo-unavailable, origin-mismatch and
603	        unreproducible classes are informational), so `converge()` is never called
604	        for one even if something recorded `APPLY` against it.
605	
606	        Before converging anything, `_record_permanent_skips` persists a `DecisionEntry`
607	        for every `SKIP_ALWAYS`-decided item (D-08). The `_finalize_unreproducible` hook
608	        then persists this run's authored snippets and unreproducible-item skip-always
609	        decisions (D-20/D-21/D-23); it is a no-op on the base and only
610	        `manual_installs_sync` implements it (D-18), but the call site stays here so both
611	        run before any converge, independent of whether this run applies anything else
612	        (a run with zero installs but one newly-authored snippet still records it). The
613	        `_unresolved_as_failures` hook (also no-op on the base, overridden only by
614	        `manual_installs_sync`) supplies the genuinely-undecided items that fail an
615	        interactive run — which is why `total == 0` can still raise `PackageItemFailures`.
616	        """
617	        assert self._accepted_plan is not None
618	        assert self._accepted_outcome is not None
619	        plan = self._accepted_plan
620	        outcome = self._accepted_outcome
621	        decisions = outcome.decisions
622	
623	        self._log_decisions(plan, decisions)
624	        await self._record_permanent_skips(plan, decisions)
625	        await self._finalize_unreproducible(plan, outcome)
626	
627	        prefix = "[dry-run] " if self.context.dry_run else ""
628	        failures: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]] = []
629	        declined: list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]] = []
630	        apply_diffs = [
631	            diff
632	            for diff in plan.diffs
633	            if decisions.get(diff.item_id) == Decision.APPLY and diff.action != DiffAction.REPORT_ONLY
634	        ]
635	
636	        total = len(apply_diffs)
637	
638	        if total == 0:
639	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}No {self.manager_id} changes to apply")
640	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
641	        else:
642	            self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.INFO, f"{prefix}Applying {total} {self.manager_id} change(s)")
643	
644	            for index, diff in enumerate(apply_diffs):
645	                self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=int(index / total * 100), item=diff.label))
646	                if self.context.dry_run:
647	                    # The detail belongs on the line, not only in the review panel: a
648	                    # dry run never renders that panel, and ADR-014 makes the preview
649	                    # the whole report. Without it the preview says strictly less about
650	                    # an item than the interactive review does.
651	                    detail = f" — {diff.detail}" if diff.detail else ""
652	                    self._log(Host.TARGET, LogLevel.FULL, f"{prefix}Would {diff.action.value} {diff.label}{detail}")
653	                else:
654	                    await self._converge_one(diff, failures, declined)
655	            self._report_progress(ProgressUpdate(percent=100))
656	
657	            succeeded = total - len(failures) - len(declined)
658	            self._log(
659	                Host.TARGET,
660	                LogLevel.INFO,
661	                f"{prefix}{succeeded}/{total} {self.manager_id} change(s) applied",
662	            )
663	
664	        # Outside the branch above: a run whose every converge declined still has to say so.
665	        if declined:
666	            summary = "; ".join(f"{diff.label}: {reason}" for diff, reason in declined)
667	            self._log(
668	                Host.TARGET,
669	                LogLevel.INFO,
670	                f"{len(declined)} {self.manager_id} change(s) not applied, by the user's answer: {summary}",
671	            )
672	
673	        all_failures = [*failures, *self._unresolved_as_failures(plan, outcome)]
674	        if all_failures:
675	            summary = "; ".join(f"{diff.label}: {stderr.strip()}" for diff, stderr in all_failures)
676	            self._log(
677	                Host.TARGET,
678	                LogLevel.INFO,
679	                f"{len(all_failures)} {self.manager_id} item(s) failed: {summary}",
680	            )
681	            raise PackageItemFailures(self.manager_id, all_failures)

683	    def _log_decisions(self, plan: PackagePlan, decisions: Mapping[str, Decision]) -> None:
684	        """One FULL line per item this job presented, naming the decision it received
685	        (`PKG-FR-LOG-DECISIONS`).
686	
687	        Every item, not only the ones that were applied: an item the user skipped produces
688	        no converge line and no report entry, so without this the log has no record that it
689	        was ever offered. The decision is written in the words the answer used rather than
690	        the enum's — "skip this run", not `skip_once` — because the log is read by the same
691	        person who answered.
692	
693	        Recorded on the machine the answer acts on, which for a removal is the target and
694	        for an install the source's intent landing on the target; both are the target, so
695	        one host label is correct for all of them.
696	
697	        Blocks are excluded: nobody was asked about one (`PKG-FR-BLOCKS-DERIVED`), so a line
698	        saying it was "reviewed" would name a question the run never put. What a block gets
699	        instead is `apply()`'s own converge line, which is what every other derived write
700	        gets (`PKG-FR-DERIVED-VISIBLE`).
701	        """
702	        for diff in plan.diffs:
703	            if diff.item_class in BLOCK_ITEM_CLASSES:
704	                continue
705	            decision = decisions.get(diff.item_id, Decision.SKIP_ONCE)
706	            self._log(
707	                Host.TARGET,
708	                LogLevel.FULL,
709	                f"reviewed {diff.label} ({diff.action.value}): {_DECISION_WORDS[decision]}",
710	            )

712	    def _unresolved_as_failures(self, plan: PackagePlan, outcome: ReviewOutcome) -> list[tuple[ItemDiff, str]]:

714	
715	        No-op on the base — it returns an empty list, so the three managers that produce
716	        no unreproducible items (apt, snap, flatpak) never fail on this basis. Only
717	        `manual_installs_sync` overrides it (D-18/D-21): an unreproducible item left with
718	        neither a snippet nor a recorded decision after an interactive review fails the
719	        job. The D-27 converge-failure contract in `apply()` is unchanged — converge
720	        failures fail the job regardless of what this hook returns.
721	        """
722	        return []

        # package half already ran over its diffs — they are derived from directory digests,
        # so no input item carried their id into `filter_inert`. The decision files
        # `_plan_packages` just read are reused rather than re-read.
        all_diffs = self._drop_inert_diffs(
            sorted(
                (*base_plan.diffs, *collateral_diffs, *repo_diffs),

    async def _plan_packages(self, origins: OriginClassifier) -> PackagePlan:
        """The package half: load decision files -> capture -> query -> diff -> build review
        groups. Read-only.

        Both machines' decision files are loaded first (a read, like everything else here)
        and each side's captured/queried items are filtered through its OWN file before
        diffing (D-08): an item recorded on the source is dropped from the source
        manifest so it is never pushed to a peer again; an item recorded on the target
        is dropped from the target query so it is never proposed for
        install/remove/change again — either way it produces no `ItemDiff` and never
        reaches the review.

        The finished diffs go through `_drop_inert_diffs` as well, which catches the
        recorded items no input-side filter can see: the `apt:hold:` membership items are
        derived from hold-set membership, and the post-diff pass is the only CORRECT place
        for them anyway — the target hold set additionally suppresses a held package's own
        install/upgrade action, so filtering that input set would re-propose upgrading a
        held package. `plan()` runs the same pass again over the repository and collateral
        diffs it appends.
        """
        self._target_installed = None
        source_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.source).load()
        target_decisions = await DecisionFile(self.manager_id, self.target).load()
        self._plan_decisions = (source_decisions, target_decisions)

        # Both files against BOTH manifests (`marks_on_either`): a package both machines
        # have must vanish from the diff entirely once either machine records it, and
        # filtering each manifest by its own file alone leaves the other machine's copy
        # unmatched — an install of a package the target already has, or a removal of one
        # the source still has.
        marked = marks_on_either(source_decisions, target_decisions)
        captured, source_origins = await self._probe.capture_source_items()
        source_items = await filter_inert(captured, marked)
        # Both manifests drop the hand-`.deb` installs `manual_installs_sync` owns before
        # anything is diffed (`PKG-FR-DEB-OWNERSHIP`), and the target's exclusion rides in
        # the same batched policy call that answers this run's origin questions.
        target_captured, policy = await self._probe.capture_target_items([item.name for item in source_items])
        target_items = await filter_inert(target_captured, marked)
        source_hold_names, target_hold_names = await self._probe.collect_hold_sets()
        await self._refuse_holds_without_their_package(source_hold_names, target_hold_names)
        origin_plan = origins.classify(source_items, target_items, policy, source_origins)
        diffs = self._drop_inert_diffs(
            diff_apt_packages(
                source_items,
                target_items,
                origin_plan,
                self.machines,
                source_hold_names,
                target_hold_names,
                self._marked_packages(source_decisions),
                self._marked_packages(target_decisions),
            ),
            source_decisions,
            target_decisions,
        )
        # `PKG-FR-APT-HOLD-VERSION`: a package the source HOLDS and the target lacks must be
        # installed at the source's own version, because the hold that follows would
        # otherwise freeze the target permanently on whatever its repositories happened to
        # offer, and nothing moves a held package again. Read off the surviving diffs so a
        # package `filter_inert` dropped cannot pin a version nothing will install.
        #
        # A held candidate enters this map whatever `dpkg-query` said about it, empty version
        # included: dropping it here is what let the install float onto whatever the target
        # offered, which the article forbids. `PackageConverger._install` refuses the empty
        # entry instead of falling back.
        source_versions = {item.name: item.version for item in source_items}

            name: source_versions[name]
            for diff in diffs
            if diff.item_class is ItemClass.APT_PACKAGE and diff.action is DiffAction.INSTALL
            for name in [package_name(diff.item_id)]
